obernants.operator: Exclude wrong modular product coefficients, overlapping-subset terms, noncanonical residues, invalid affine particular/nullspace certificates or a nonleast/incorrect discrete exponent. Exclude replacing field residues with raw floating magnitudes or equating resource refusal with algebraic None.

obernants.operator: Ideal fixed-size DFT is invertible; rounded FFT can merge input bit patterns. Polynomial product admits factor scaling(a*c,b/c) and zero-product ambiguity. Subset output with fixed a and a[empty]!=0 uniquely recovers b in the field, while zero a admits every b. Gaussian output admits many row-equivalent systems. BSGS Some0 admits every base with target1, and modular normalization makes raw representatives nonunique.

obernants.operator: Zero-pad real coefficient vectors to power2 length at least len(a)+len(b)-1, transform, pointwise multiply, inverse, and compare small integer coefficients with Karatsuba modulo p. Without padding the FFT gives circular convolution. A measured small-fixture error permits rounding only there; no blanket exact field recovery follows for arbitrary coefficients or cancellation.
